\section[de pronto]{de pronto — suddenly}

\label{lesson:ES-C534-de-pronto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for unexpected, then the Spanish for sudden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: de pronto}
\textbf{de pronto} — \textquotedblleft{}suddenly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
De pronto se apagaron las luces.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Suddenly the lights went out.}
\end{quote}

The same as \emph{de repente}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{de pronto} is built on \emph{pronto}, which comes from Latin \emph{promptus} 'brought forth, ready' (EtymDB). \emph{De pronto} is the moment something is ready to happen and happens.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{de pronto}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{de pronto}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{de pronto}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for unexpected, then the Spanish for sudden, then say \emph{de pronto} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does de pronto mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Suddenly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[súbitamente]{súbitamente — all of a sudden, suddenly}

\label{lesson:ES-C534-subitamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for sudden, then the Spanish for suddenly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: súbitamente}
\textbf{súbitamente} — \textquotedblleft{}all of a sudden, suddenly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Súbitamente se abrió la puerta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Suddenly the door opened.}
\end{quote}

A written word; in speech, \emph{de repente} or \emph{de pronto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{súbitamente} is built on \emph{súbito} 'sudden' and the ending \emph{-mente}. \emph{Súbito} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{subitus} 'sudden' (EtymDB), from \emph{subīre} 'to come up', built on \emph{sub} and \emph{īre} 'to go'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{súbitamente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{súbitamente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{súbitamente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for sudden, then the Spanish for suddenly, then say \emph{súbitamente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does súbitamente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}All of a sudden, suddenly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[inmediatamente]{inmediatamente — immediately}

\label{lesson:ES-C534-inmediatamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for suddenly, then the Spanish for all of a sudden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: inmediatamente}
\textbf{inmediatamente} — \textquotedblleft{}immediately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Llamé inmediatamente a la policía.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I immediately called the police.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Enseguida} is a more everyday word for it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inmediatamente} is built on \emph{inmediato} and the ending \emph{-mente} (EtymDB). \emph{Inmediato} is a learned word from Latin \emph{immediātus} 'with nothing in the middle', from \emph{medius} 'middle'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inmediatamente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inmediatamente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{inmediatamente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for suddenly, then the Spanish for all of a sudden, then say \emph{inmediatamente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does inmediatamente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Immediately\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[a continuación]{a continuación — next, then; below}

\label{lesson:ES-C534-a-continuacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for all of a sudden, then the Spanish for immediately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a continuación}
\textbf{a continuación} — \textquotedblleft{}next, then; below\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A continuación, el ladrón salió por la ventana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Next, the thief went out through the window.}
\end{quote}

In a text it means below: \emph{Lea las instrucciones que aparecen a continuación.}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{a continuación} is built on \emph{continuación}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{continuātiō} 'an unbroken series, a following of one thing after another' (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{continuus} 'joined, unbroken'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a continuación}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a continuación}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for all of a sudden, then the Spanish for immediately, then say \emph{a continuación} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[bruscamente]{bruscamente — abruptly, sharply}

\label{lesson:ES-C534-bruscamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for immediately, then the Spanish for next.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: bruscamente}
\textbf{bruscamente} — \textquotedblleft{}abruptly, sharply\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El autobús frenó bruscamente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The bus braked sharply.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Brusco} also describes a rude manner: \emph{una respuesta brusca}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bruscamente} is built on \emph{brusco} 'abrupt' and the ending \emph{-mente}. \emph{Brusco} was borrowed from Italian \emph{brusco} 'sharp, sour' (EtymDB), whose own origin is less certain.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bruscamente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bruscamente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bruscamente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for immediately, then the Spanish for next, then say \emph{bruscamente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
